deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a field, k'/k a finite extension, and C is a k-linear ⊗-category that is associative, unital and commutative ('AUC'). Grothendieck first wrote 'foncteur fibre', struck it, and replaced it with an exact, faithful, k-linear ⊗-functor F : C → Modf(k'), with values in finite-dimensional k'-vector spaces. Rigidity is not assumed, so this is a non-neutral Tannaka situation where the fibre functor lands over a larger field. He claims the pair (C, F) is equivalent to the following data.

1°) An affine k'-scheme G' with a k'-point ε. Equivalently, a commutative k'-algebra U with an augmentation ε : U → k'.

2°) Let A = Ǔ := Hom_{k'}(U, k'), the pro-finite-dimensional dual of U. Viewed as a pro-object of Modf(k) (k-linear, not k'-linear), A carries an associative ring structure with unit ε. Concretely, A is the pro-ring End(F) of endomorphisms of the fibre functor seen as a k-linear functor. It is subject to two conditions:
(i) The map k' → A, λ ↦ λε, is multiplicative. So A is a pro-k-algebra containing k', but k' need not be central.
(ii) The k'-linear map Δ : A → A ⊗̂_{k'} A, the transpose of multiplication in U, is 'multiplicative' in the following sense. Let 𝒥 = Ker(k'⊗_k k' → k') be the augmentation ideal, and J = 𝒥·(A ⊗̂_k A). Let J̃ = {λ ∈ A ⊗̂_k A : λJ ⊂ J} be the idealizer of J. Then J̃/J ⊂ (A⊗̂_k A)/J = A ⊗̂_{k'} A is a ring. The condition is that Δ takes values in J̃/J and is a ring homomorphism A → J̃/J.

In modern terms, J̃/J is exactly Takeuchi's ×_R-product A ×_{k'} A, a subring of A ⊗_{k'} A. So (A, Δ, ε) is the pro-dual of a k'-bialgebroid, i.e. a Takeuchi ×_{k'}-bialgebra. The commutative k'-algebra U is the coordinate ring of the k'-'fibre' of the (monoidal) groupoid acting on Spec k' over k. The noncentral embedding k' ⊂ A records the second anchor.

This is a Tannaka reconstruction for k'-valued fibre functors in the language of bialgebroids. It is equivalent to Deligne's k'/k-groupoid over Spec(k'⊗_k k') in 'Catégories tannakiennes' (1990), but phrased via a one-sided affine scheme over k' plus a ring structure on its dual. The working title 'Rigidité' suggests the following pages treat when C is rigid, i.e. when the bialgebroid is a Hopf algebroid or groupoid.
errors: The list of conditions is incomplete on this page. Coassociativity and counitality of Δ with respect to ε are not stated, nor the compatibility of the ⊗-unit and symmetry constraints with commutativity of U. They may have been intended for later pages.

The equivalence as stated needs an essential-image description. C should be recovered as the category of continuous A-modules (equivalently U-comodule-type objects) of finite k'-dimension. It also requires abelianness or Karoubian-type hypotheses on C; otherwise it holds only up to completion.
The idealizer J̃ and the quotient J̃/J are taken inside a completed pro-tensor product. Making 'idealizer' meaningful for pro-objects requires care with the topologies, and this is glossed over.

The k'-linearity conventions are ambiguous: on which side of A ⊗_{k'} A k' acts on each factor (the left/right bimodule structure) is not specified. Takeuchi's definition requires this to be specified precisely.

ideas.what: Tannakian reconstruction for an exact faithful ⊗-functor with values in Modf(k') for a finite extension k'/k (non-neutral case)
ideas.modern_name: Non-neutral Tannaka duality / fibre functor over S = Spec k'; transitive k'/k-groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972, flawed in the non-neutral case), Deligne 'Catégories tannakiennes' (1990)
ideas.where_published: The Tannakian idea is attributed to Grothendieck via Saavedra. This bialgebroid formulation is not in his published texts as far as I know.

ideas.what: Encoding the structure via the dual pro-ring A = End(F) containing k' noncentrally, with comultiplication valued in the idealizer quotient J̃/J ⊂ A⊗_{k'}A
ideas.modern_name: Takeuchi ×_R-product; ×_R-bialgebra = (left) bialgebroid; Tannaka duality for bialgebroids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sweedler (1974) and Takeuchi (1977) for ×_R-bialgebras; Lu (1996), Bruguières (1994), Day–Street, Szlachányi (2009), Phùng Hồ Hải (2008) for the Tannakian link

ideas.what: Description by a one-sided augmented commutative k'-algebra U (affine k'-scheme G' with section) instead of a groupoid over Spec(k'⊗_k k')
ideas.modern_name: Fibre at the base point of the Tannakian groupoid / k'-bialgebroid with commutative 'total' algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne 1990 and in the Hopf algebroid literature

missed.claim: Around or after 1984, Grothendieck formulates Tannaka reconstruction for k'-valued fibre functors in terms of a pro-ring A ⊃ k' (k' noncentral) with a coproduct landing in the idealizer quotient J̃/J. This is precisely Takeuchi's ×_{k'}-product and the bialgebroid structure, independently of the Hopf-algebroid/Tannaka literature (Bruguières 1994, Szlachányi 2009) and predating Deligne 1990.
missed.quote: prend ses valeurs dans J̃/J ... J = 𝒥.(A ⊗̂_k A) ... J̃ = {λ ∈ A ⊗̂_k A | λJ ⊂ J}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precedent: Grothendieck was independently using the ×_R-bialgebra device in a Tannakian context. Mathematically, the results are now known (bialgebroid Tannaka duality).

missed.claim: The title suggests a treatment of rigidity, i.e. when the dual pro-bialgebroid admits an antipode, in the non-rigid, non-neutral setting. That is not visible on this page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only minor: rigidity criteria for bialgebroid-Tannakian categories are already known (Schauenburg, Bruguières, Szlachányi).

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck independently arrives at the Takeuchi ×_{k'}-product (idealizer construction) and a bialgebroid description of non-neutral fibre functors, around the time of or before Deligne 1990. This is a notable unpublished detail, but the mathematics itself is now standard in the bialgebroid/Tannaka literature.
transcription_corrections: 'une structure d'anneau connexe[?]' is more plausibly 'une structure d'anneau associatif' (with unit ε).
'dans J̃/J (anneau) où' should read roughly 'dans J̃/J ⊂ A ⊗̂_{k'} A (J = 𝒥.(A ⊗̂_k A), idéal ...)', with 'anneau' written under J̃/J.
The marginal note on the left is '(Comp.)', apparently marking condition (ii) as the compatibility (multiplicativity) condition.
The last line reads roughly 'et à cette fin est multiplicative' / 'homomorphisme A → J̃/J'.
'idéal d'augm. par 𝒥 = Ker(k'⊗_k k' → k')': 𝒥 is the augmentation ideal of k'⊗_k k'.
